fact_check_rounds.label: Round 1: designed sample of 30 plants (all High, all customer plants, then by score), before repairs
Round 2: 10 unsampled plants from multi-plant parents, after the first repair pass
Round 3: all 23 plants no checker had seen, after the attribution clean-up
Round 4: 32 plants added or changed by the first higher-tier review, after the attribution clean-up
Round 5: 9 plants whose points changed in the final higher-tier review, plus 6 new addresses

miss_rate.value: Auditor-measured 8/58 = 13.8% (6 never found, 2 found but wrongly excluded); finder first pass 31/89 = 34.8% (22 never found = 24.7%; 9 found but wrongly excluded = 10.1%)
miss_rate.note: Auditor-measured: of the 58 in-definition plants the two list auditors found (now included), 8 were not on the plant-finder's included list. It is a lower bound: the auditors used the finder's kinds of sources. First pass: of all 89 plants now included, 31 were not on the finder's included list: 22 it never found (7 auditors, 2 follow-up research, 13 higher-tier reviews and lead close-out) and 9 it found but excluded although the inclusion rule includes them. All are in the ledger now. Leads closed 2026-11-13: 17 checked (1 included, 10 excluded, 6 unverified with what was tried); 1 new lead open: a possible MICA Steelworks welding site at Euless TX.

known_limits: Part size is unknown for 69 of 81 profiled plants, so material scores 0 there; a Low score usually means missing data, not a poor fit (see the Unknowns and ceiling columns).

Welder-posting counts are a snapshot of 2026-11-13 job boards. Sabre's board files every requisition in a city under one address with several site codes, so Sabre postings are tied to a plant only where the city has one Sabre plant; FWT Fort Worth's are not counted.
Pre-production plants (Nucor Brigham City ramping, Hapco Oklahoma City under construction) are scored on stated plans; Nucor's Indiana pole plant (Crawfordsville) is operating.
8 plants included by the DOT-listing rule or the lead close-out are base records, not profiled or scored.
Opening lines are composed from stated claims; the round-5 line check corrected 16 of 98 lines (9 for a fact, 7 for the closing question) and the corrections are applied.
Fact-check error rates are per claim checked; on a strict page-only reading (every clause on the one cited page) round 4 would be higher (checker A: 16.0% vs 6.4%).
